children.name: Grubbia rourkei Carlquist
children.description: A South African endemic shrub of the family Grubbiaceae (order Cornales), described by Carlquist in 1977. An ericoid, leathery-leaved fynbos shrub, it is a high-altitude habitat specialist restricted to the Kogelberg (Western Cape), growing in Kogelberg Sandstone Fynbos on damp sandstone slopes. SANBI Red List: Rare (known from fewer than five sites, population stable).

children.name: Grubbia tomentosa  Harms
children.description: An evergreen, multi-stemmed shrublet up to ~1.5 m (Koolhout), resprouting from a fire-resistant woody stump, with opposite leathery narrowly elliptical leaves whose margins roll under, cone-like axillary clusters of pinkish flowers, and a reddish-purple berry-like fruit. A South African endemic of the family Grubbiaceae, confined to fynbos on drier rocky sandstone slopes of the western Cape. SANBI Red List: Least Concern.
